examples.scenario: Two semantically equal JSON objects arrive with different property order and whitespace
examples.reason: Hashing noncanonical text would produce different digests.

examples.scenario: A JSON object repeats the same property name three times
examples.reason: Default parsers may silently retain only the final value.

examples.scenario: A manifest contains NaN and the encoder emits a JavaScript extension
examples.reason: NaN and Infinity are outside interoperable JSON and JCS input constraints.

examples.scenario: The same numeric array is hashed once in C order and once in Fortran order
examples.reason: Memory traversal order changes the raw byte sequence.

examples.scenario: A native-endian int16 array moves from little-endian to big-endian hardware
A file keeps the same name and size but one byte changes during transfer
examples.reason: Names and lengths alone cannot prove byte identity.

examples.scenario: Two environments report the same Python version but different NumPy wheel and compiler builds
examples.reason: Interpreter version alone is not a sufficient replay identity.

examples.scenario: A clean replay produces equal values but a different canonical evidence-bundle digest
examples.reason: Unexplained evidence differences prevent deterministic acceptance.
